matched_pairs.b_evidence_quote: we introduce novel Region Proposal Networks (RPNs) that share convolutional layers with state-of-the-art object detection networks
we introduce novel "anchor" boxes that serve as references at multiple scales and aspect ratios.
ours is a two-stage cascade consisting of class-agnostic proposals and class-specific detections.
we adopt non-maximum suppression (NMS) on the proposal regions based on their cls scores. We fix the IoU threshold for NMS at 0.7
The RoI pooling layer [2] in Fast R-CNN accepts the convolutional features and also the predicted bounding boxes as input
we minimize an objective function following the multi-task loss in Fast R-CNN [2]. Our loss function for an image is defined as: L({pi},{ti}) = 1/Ncls ∑ Lcls + λ 1/Nreg ∑ p*i Lreg
We present more results on the Microsoft COCO object detection dataset [12].

matched_pairs.b_rationale: The article introduces and relies on anchor boxes; it does not use or discuss anchor-free detection.
The article does not use bipartite/Hungarian matching or direct set prediction; it uses NMS-based proposal selection.
The article uses convolutional networks; no transformer encoder-decoder architecture is used or discussed.
The article uses smooth L1 and log loss; focal loss is not mentioned.
The article focuses on object detection with bounding boxes; no mask prediction branch is introduced.
ROIAlign is not mentioned; the article uses RoI pooling from Fast R-CNN.
Compound scaling of depth/width/resolution is not discussed in this article.
